newsitem.title: USA: Sugen files tumor treatment IND.
newsitem.headline: Sugen files tumor treatment IND.

text.p: Sugen Inc said Wednesday that it has filed an Investigational New Drug (IND) application with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for the clinical testing of a potential treatment for tumors.

Sugen said it filed an IND for a synthetic small molecule signal transduction inhibitor of Flk-1/KDR that has therapeutic potential as an anti-angiogenesis and anti-metastasis agent in solid tumor cancer patients.
Angiogenesis is the process by which tumors trigger the new blood vessel formation needed for their nourishment, growth and metastasis.

Sugen said its target validation studies have implicated Flk-1 as a primary driver of angiogenesis in the majority of solid tumors and have shown also that this receptor may play a critical role in metastatic disease processes.
If the clinical development were successful, it is currently anticipated that this drug candidate could be brought to market in both injectable and oral formulations.
